title: aquaBOT
subtitle: An interactive 3D playground for a custom 6-DOF robot arm.
description: Explore the aquaBOT in your browser: orbit the model, adjust individual joints, control the parallel-jaw gripper, and experiment with poses in a Frutiger Aero-inspired interface.

specs.label: Robot
specs.value: 6-DOF arm with parallel-jaw gripper

specs.label: Model
specs.value: Fusion parts with URDF joint definitions

specs.label: Controls
specs.value: Joint sliders, gripper, and animation

specs.label: Export
specs.value: Copy poses as JSON

sections.title: Design language
sections.body: Aero explores a friendlier visual identity for a desktop robot: translucent aqua shells, pearl structural parts, and large circular joints. The underwater interface carries that early-2000s consumer-electronics influence into the browser, giving the robot a playful setting in which to explore its movement.

sections.title: From CAD to the browser
sections.body: The viewer combines Fusion part geometry with URDF joint definitions. Six rotational controls follow the arm from base yaw through wrist roll, while the gripper control moves the parallel jaws. The model can be inspected from any angle using orbit, zoom, and a top-view camera.

sections.title: Movement & interaction
sections.body: Manual sliders let each joint and the gripper be explored independently. Playback animates the arm, reset returns it to its starting pose, and the copy action exports the current joint values as JSON. This is a visual playground: CAD limits are provisional and no collision prevention or hardware control is provided.

references: Interactive viewer built from Fusion parts and URDF joint definitions.
disclosures: CAD joint limits are provisional. The playground does not control hardware or prevent collisions.

title: RIGBY
subtitle: Low-cost mobile bimanual platform for assistive manipulation learned from demonstration.
description: A complete embodied robotics project investigating whether useful mobile manipulation behaviours can be taught and deployed on affordable hardware without relying on high-cost research platforms.

specs.label: Cost
specs.value: £1,951 complete mobile platform

specs.label: Manipulation
specs.value: 7-DOF dominant arm + 5-DOF support arm

specs.label: Learning
specs.value: ACT baseline and custom DOM-ACT architecture

specs.label: Deployment
specs.value: LeRobot inference on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano

sections.title: System
sections.body: Built RIGBY as an integrated mobile manipulation platform spanning mechanical design, actuation, sensing, onboard compute, power distribution, control software and autonomous policy deployment.

sections.title: Mechanical Design
sections.body: Developed an asymmetric bimanual configuration with additional dexterity assigned to the dominant arm. I designed the 7-DOF manipulator and parallel-jaw grippers, iterating link geometry and distal mass while preserving workspace, grasp reliability and wrist-camera visibility.

sections.title: Teleoperation
sections.body: Built a whole-body leader-follower teleoperation system using two leader arms for manipulation and rudder pedals for the mobile base. Arm, gripper and base actions were recorded simultaneously through LeRobot to produce demonstrations for imitation learning.

sections.title: Simulation
sections.body: Created the robot's URDF and MJCF models from the physical CAD geometry, validating link dimensions, masses, inertias, joint limits and camera frames against the hardware to support simulation and future learning-based research.

sections.title: Learning
sections.body: Used Action Chunking with Transformers as the imitation-learning baseline and proposed DOM-ACT, which conditions support-arm and mobile-base predictions on features from the dominant manipulation plan. On a sequential bimanual task, success increased from 65% with ACT to 80% with DOM-ACT.

sections.title: Interaction
sections.body: Developed a multimodal web interface for task selection, demonstration recording, training configuration and policy execution. The same interface supported touchscreen, text and voice interaction, with perception-assisted task discovery used to match recognised objects to available trained behaviours.

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.body: Evaluated the system on pen placement, wine-glass lifting and wiping, Ziploc closure and chair repositioning. The experiments compared task success, completion time and motion smoothness while also exposing practical limits from actuator quality, environment-specific imitation learning and onboard control frequency.

title: CHARIS
subtitle: Low-cost assistive robot for accessible play and child-centred interaction.
description: A team-built robotic companion for children with motor disabilities, combining accessible control, computer vision, autonomous behaviours, and adaptive interactive games.

specs.label: Role
specs.value: Project Manager and Software Developer

specs.label: Interaction
specs.value: Head tracking, adaptive controllers, and GUI

specs.label: Perception
specs.value: OpenCV, MediaPipe, object detection, and LiDAR

specs.label: Platform
specs.value: Modified low-cost XLeRobot mobile manipulator

sections.title: Intent
sections.body: CHARIS explored how low-cost robotics could make play and everyday interaction more accessible for children with motor disabilities through intuitive controls, adaptive games, and assistive autonomous behaviours.

sections.title: Build
sections.body: Led the project team and developed the frontend stack, including a modular child-friendly interface, real-time adaptive difficulty model, and OpenCV/MediaPipe head tracking, integrated with the wider ROS 2 robotic system.

title: TFLBot
subtitle: Assistive guidance robot for underground transport networks.
description: A human-centred robotics project extending a SoftBank Pepper with autonomous navigation, LiDAR perception, multimodal interaction, and synchronised speech and gesture for accessible passenger guidance.

specs.label: Platform
specs.value: SoftBank Pepper with upgraded sensing and compute

specs.label: Navigation
specs.value: LiDAR mapping, collision avoidance, and autonomous guidance

specs.label: Interaction
specs.value: Speech, gesture, touchscreen, multilingual, and BSL

specs.label: Result
specs.value: Mean cognitive load reduced from 2.0 to 1.4

sections.title: Robot
sections.body: Extended Pepper with a Jetson Orin Nano, Orbbec RGB-D camera, ReSpeaker microphone array, RPLIDAR A2M12, and custom mounts, overcoming limitations in the robot's onboard perception and compute.

sections.title: Task
sections.body: TFLBot explored whether an embodied robot could make underground navigation more accessible by combining physical guidance with speech, visual feedback, multilingual interaction, and British Sign Language support.

sections.title: Control
sections.body: Implemented LiDAR collision avoidance using DBSCAN obstacle clustering and built occupancy maps from scan-matched odometry. I also developed a library of deictic gestures through kinaesthetic teaching and synchronised them with spoken guidance.

sections.title: Results
sections.body: A comparative user study evaluated no aid, stationary robotic guidance, and mobile guidance. The mobile robot reduced mean cognitive load from 2.0 to 1.4 and achieved the highest satisfaction, although conservative navigation substantially increased completion time.

references: Project assets include system architecture, perception, navigation, interaction, and evaluation results.
disclosures: Academic team project completed at Imperial College London.
TfL is referenced as the transport-service context; TFLBot is an academic prototype and not an official TfL product.

title: ChessBot
subtitle: Analytical kinematics, workspace calibration, and trajectory control for a 4-DOF manipulator.
description: A robotics project taking a 4-DOF arm from analytical modelling to physical task execution through closed-form inverse kinematics, empirical workspace calibration, trajectory generation, and a custom task-specific gripper.

specs.label: Robot
specs.value: 4-DOF Dynamixel manipulator

specs.label: Kinematics
specs.value: DH forward and closed-form inverse kinematics

specs.label: Calibration
specs.value: Measured workspace correction using RBF interpolation

specs.label: Planning
specs.value: Task-specific Cartesian trajectory generation

sections.title: Experience
sections.body: The system translated Cartesian task points into physical manipulation sequences, coordinating approach, grasp, transfer, and release motions across several tasks while compensating for the difference between the ideal kinematic model and the real robot.

sections.title: Engineering
sections.body: Derived the DH model and closed-form inverse kinematics, validated them in MATLAB, and deployed them to Dynamixel hardware. I then built Python tools for trajectory generation and empirical workspace calibration, using measured errors to correct commanded positions before execution.

title: Options Market Making Algorithm
subtitle: Delta-aware trading strategy ranked 3rd in an Imperial Optiver competition.
description: A Python market-making strategy combining order-book fair-value estimation, Black–Scholes option pricing, inventory and delta-aware quote sizing, and opportunistic arbitrage, ranking 3rd out of roughly 100 participants.

specs.label: Result
specs.value: 3rd / ~100 participants

specs.label: Pricing
specs.value: Order-book fair value + Black–Scholes option pricing

specs.label: Risk
specs.value: Delta- and position-aware dynamic quote sizing

specs.label: Execution
specs.value: Passive market making with opportunistic arbitrage

sections.title: Strategy
sections.body: Estimated the underlying fair value from weighted bid and ask information, then used Black–Scholes to price related options. The difference between estimated fair value and the market price was converted into a confidence signal used to adjust quote size and exposure.

sections.title: Risk
sections.body: Rather than repeatedly trading back to delta neutrality, the strategy incorporated portfolio delta and total position into subsequent bid and ask volumes. This allowed it to continuously provide liquidity while steering inventory back toward a market-neutral position.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.body: The strategy ranked 3rd in a field of roughly 100 participants. Delta and PnL monitoring were used throughout development to tune the quoting logic, with most performance generated by the passive strategy rather than active arbitrage.
